meanings.note: Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'decade / ten' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Elya, I am in my fifties.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть десяток.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always decade.

Core Russian prep meaning 'until, before; up to' in everyday speech.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'втра').

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

meanings.note: In the sky. Common feminine noun meaning 'star; celebrity' in everyday Russian.
Common feminine noun meaning 'star; celebrity' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: There are bright stars in the sky.

examples.text: Вот молодёжь, ничего не знают! Это же Лещенко! Звезда!
examples.trans: Young people these days, they don't know anything! That's Leshchenko! A star!

meanings.en: to get acquainted, to meet (someone new)
meanings.note: 'Давайте знакомиться' = let's introduce ourselves

examples.text: Очень хорошо. Ну что, давайте знакомиться.
examples.trans: Very good. Well then, let's introduce everyone.

meanings.note: In one direction, now. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to go (on foot)', paired with 'пойти'.

examples.trans: He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Core Russian conj meaning 'or' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: мам! = casual 'Mum!' when calling her

examples.text: Что за меню здесь? Как позвонить?
examples.trans: What's this menu here? How do I make a call?

meanings.note: Plural 'мозги' in everyday speech. Common masculine noun meaning 'brain' in everyday Russian.
Plural 'мозги' in everyday speech. Common masculine noun meaning 'brain' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: There are brains, but no money.

examples.text: В Москве вам дают деньги на дорогую одежду, а мозги не дают.
examples.trans: In Moscow they give you money for expensive clothes, but they don't give you brains.

meanings.note: Agrees with the thing owned. Core Russian det meaning 'my, mine' in everyday speech.
нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'we' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
Core Russian num meaning 'both' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: You both leave here right now.
Get over here right now, quickly, both of you!

examples.text: Вы сейчас отсюда оба уходите. И больше сюда не возвращаетесь. Ясно?
examples.trans: You both leave here right now. And you never come back here again. Clear?

meanings.note: Firm promise or requirement. Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'язательно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Государство обязательно увидит и назначит операцию.
examples.trans: The state will surely see and will schedule the surgery.
I'll definitely buy you a tank.

meanings.note: Остаётся у нас = stays with us. Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to stay, to remain', paired with 'остаться'.

examples.trans: And the advance stays with us.

meanings.note: ничего не осталось = there's nothing left

Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to remain, to be left', paired with 'оставаться'.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: ты ещё пожалеешь! = you'll be sorry!

+ accusative. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'жалеть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to regret; to feel sorry', paired with 'жалеть'.

examples.text: Ты знаешь, сколько у меня денег? Ты ещё пожалеешь!
examples.trans: Do you know how much money I have? You'll be sorry!

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'лучить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to get, to receive', paired with 'получать'.

examples.text: А кто их получит? Те, кто сидит повыше?
examples.trans: And who will get it? The people who sit higher up?

meanings.note: Последний раз = for the last time. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'следний'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('last, final').

examples.trans: I'm asking for the last time.
I'm asking for the last time. Where is the money?

meanings.note: 'будут проблемы' = there'll be trouble

examples.trans: I know the problems of ordinary people.

meanings.note: Dining establishment. Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.

examples.trans: They called from the Italian restaurant.
In the evening they went to a restaurant.

examples.text: Кстати, звонили из итальянского ресторана. Дарят папе романтический ужин на двоих.
examples.trans: By the way, they called from the Italian restaurant. They're giving Dad a romantic dinner for two.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: Reflexive; no nominative. Core Russian pron meaning 'oneself' in everyday speech.

examples.text: А с Пашей я снова чувствую себя женщиной.
examples.trans: And with Pasha I feel like a woman again.

meanings.note: Что случилось? = what happened?. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лучиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to happen', paired with 'случаться'.

examples.text: Марина, я вам обещаю: со стеной ничего не случится.
examples.trans: Marina, I promise you: nothing will happen to the wall.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'уббота'). Common feminine noun meaning 'Saturday' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Скажи всем, что в субботу будет вечеринка.
examples.trans: Tell everyone that on Saturday there will be a party.

examples.text: Скажи всем ребятам, что в субботу вечером будет вечеринка.
examples.trans: Tell all the guys that on Saturday evening there will be a party.

examples.text: Каждую субботу в нашем ресторане бронируют абсолютно все столики.
examples.trans: Every Saturday absolutely all the tables in our restaurant are booked.

meanings.note: A whole portion; completed action. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ъесть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to eat (up)', paired with 'есть'.

examples.text: Скоро. А пока я есть хочу, слона бы съел!
examples.trans: Soon. But for now I'm hungry, I could eat an elephant!

meanings.note: softens a request: только не сердись = just don't be angry
One person, informal. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'at, by; (у меня) I have' in everyday speech.

Просить у кого. Core Russian prep meaning 'at, by; (у меня) I have' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Уволен = fired (short participle). Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'волить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to fire, to dismiss', paired with 'увольнять'.

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'вольняться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'quit, resign'.

examples.trans: And I am quitting in the meantime.

examples.text: Если вы мне не верите, то я прямо сейчас увольняюсь!
examples.trans: If you do not believe me, then I am quitting right now!

examples.text: Никто из поваров не хотел увольняться из команды Баринова.
examples.trans: None of the cooks wanted to resign from Barinov's team.

meanings.note: Often plural: условия. Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'словие'). Common neuter noun meaning 'condition' in everyday Russian.
Of an agreement. Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'словие'). Common neuter noun meaning 'condition' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Look what the conditions are like here.

examples.text: Посмотрите, какие тут условия. В эту комнату, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: Look what the conditions are like here. Into this room, please.

meanings.en: to leave, to go away (on foot)
meanings.note: Уходи! = Go away!. Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'ходить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to leave, to go away', paired with 'уйти'.
How something is done. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: У меня есть шанс = I have a chance. From French 'chance' (favorable turn of the dice, from Late Latin 'cadentia').

examples.text: А у меня все шансы есть. Жена, двое детей, не сидел, служил в армии.
examples.trans: And I've got every chance. A wife, two kids, no prison record, I served in the army.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian cardinal or ordinal numeral meaning 'sixth', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Elya, I am in my fifties.

examples.text: Костя сказал это совершенно шестой и спокойно.
examples.trans: Kostya said this quite sixth and calmly.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Linking word: главное — это народ. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!
